# Reader Guide and Prerequisites {.unnumbered}

*Physical AI Systems* is written as an independent, self-contained textbook for advanced undergraduate students, graduate researchers, and practicing systems engineers who wish to build machines that safely couple learned intelligence to physical matter and energy.

Readers arrive from different engineering disciplines, with the primary audience being computer science and electrical engineering students with a strong background in Machine Learning Systems. This guide delineates the assumed technical baseline from material developed within this book, and outlines reading pathways tailored to different engineering backgrounds.

## The Technical Starting Point {#sec-prereq-baseline}

The curriculum is designed for readers transitioning from digital computing disciplines into physical embodiment. The primary audience arrives with deep fluency in machine learning systems, computer architecture, systems programming, and linear algebra. This book assumes **zero prior background** in robotics kinematics, mechanical design, or classical control theory; all physical dynamics, power electronics, real-time safety barriers, and execution architectures are derived strictly from first principles.

### What the machine learning systems student brings

Readers emerging from modern machine learning systems curricula—such as the CS 288 sequence or foundational courses in machine learning systems—bring five core engineering competencies:

* **Deep Learning Frameworks and Computational Graphs (Foundational MLSys Baseline)**: Mastery of PyTorch and JAX tensor operations, automatic differentiation (autograd reverse-mode graph construction), operator scheduling, and common neural architectures (Transformers, multi-head attention, KV-cache paging, convolutional vision backbones, and diffusion or flow-matching decoders). Readers understand operator fusion and compiler toolchains (such as TorchDynamo, Accelerated Linear Algebra (XLA), and Triton), profiling compute-bound versus memory-bandwidth-bound kernels.
* **Systems Programming and Operating System Concurrency (Systems Infrastructure Baseline)**: Fluency in C, C++, or Rust; POSIX threads, shared-memory inter-process communication (IPC), ring buffers, atomic primitives, memory barriers, cache coherence, OS scheduling, event loops, and zero-copy socket buffers.
* **Linear Algebra, Vector Calculus, and Numerical Methods (Mathematical Baseline)**: Matrix decompositions (SVD, QR, Cholesky), vector calculus, coordinate frame rotations (SO(3), SE(3)), affine transforms, gradient descent optimization, and constrained optimization using Lagrange multipliers.
* **Computer Architecture and Accelerator Memory Hierarchies (Hardware Systems Baseline)**: Deep understanding of modern processor and accelerator hierarchies: general-purpose CPUs, discrete GPUs, and dedicated neural processing units (NPUs). Readers know how to profile execution using the Roofline model ($y = \min(\text{Peak FLOP/s}, \text{Peak BW} \times I)$) across on-chip SRAM, low-power DDR (LPDDR), and high-bandwidth memory (HBM), analyzing memory bandwidth limits and arithmetic intensity.
* **Distributed Systems and Fleet Scaling (Distributed MLSys Baseline)**: Working knowledge of distributed training and inference clusters, collective communication primitives (AllReduce, AllGather, ReduceScatter), 3D parallelism (tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism), ZeRO memory optimization, and low-latency interconnects (InfiniBand, RoCE).

### Digital systems assumptions to unlearn: The transition bridge

While these five competencies provide an indispensable technical foundation, digital computing instills implicit systems assumptions that directly contradict the physical realities of embodied autonomy. Crossing into physical AI requires explicitly unlearning five digital conventions:

* **The Infinitely Compliant Substrate vs. Irreversible Electromagnetic Work**: Digital software treats silicon as an abstract arithmetic substrate that executes instructions without physical wear or thermal danger. In physical AI, software directly commands three-phase inverters that drive physical phase currents ($I_{\text{phase}}$), dissipating irreversible Joule heat ($P = I_{\text{phase}}^2 R_{\text{phase}}$) in motor windings and inducing steep inductive voltage sag ($V_{\text{sag}} = L_{\text{cable}} \frac{di}{dt}$) on DC battery rails.
* **Batching Across Time ($B \gg 1$) vs. Strictly Non-Batchable Execution ($B = 1$)**: Digital serving packs tokens and user queries into massive batches to saturate systolic tensor arrays and amortize memory bandwidth. In physical AI, batching across future time steps is physically impossible: batch size collapses strictly to $B=1$ because every executed action modifies the physical plant state and dictates future sensory observations ($s_{t+1} \sim P(s \mid s_t, a_t)$).
* **Pipelining as Free Throughput vs. Phase Lag Instability**: In digital ML, multi-stage pipelines (pipeline parallelism, asynchronous micro-batching) hide latency behind compute throughput. In physical closed-loop control, pipelining introduces pure delay ($\tau_{\text{delay}}$) and phase lag ($\phi = -\omega \tau_{\text{delay}}$), eroding the phase margin of feedback loops and transforming stable negative feedback into divergent physical oscillation and mechanical resonance.
* **Average-Case and Tail-Tolerant Latency vs. Hard Real-Time Deadlines**: In digital web services, p50 and p90 latencies govern user satisfaction, while rare p99 tail spikes are absorbed by queueing or client retries. In physical embodiment, an unhandled tail latency spike means missing a hard 20 ms control deadline, leaving a fast-moving physical plant unguided under momentum.
* **Software Reversibility vs. Irreversible Mechanical Yield**: In digital computing, errors are caught by exception handlers, transactions are rolled back, and node crashes are recovered by reloading checkpoints from persistent storage. In physical AI, once motor torque shears gear teeth in a non-backdrivable harmonic drive or an autonomous chassis collides with an obstacle, software cannot issue an undo or reload a checkpoint.

### What you will master: The physical AI frontier

Physical AI terminates digital software forgiveness. When a learned policy issues commands across the causal boundary into physical actuators, the machine encounters physical conservation laws and hard real-time deadlines that cannot be solved by expanding model capacity or training datasets. This textbook develops the physical, computational, and architectural principles required to master these realities:

* **Continuous Plant Dynamics, Non-Backdrivable Gearboxes, and Reflected Rotor Inertia**: Moving from discrete token sequences to continuous differential equations ($\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{q})\ddot{\mathbf{q}} + \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{q}, \dot{\mathbf{q}})\dot{\mathbf{q}} + \mathbf{g}(\mathbf{q}) = \boldsymbol{\tau}$). Understanding why reflected rotor inertia scales quadratically with the gear reduction ratio ($J_{\text{ref}} = N^2 J_{\text{rotor}}$), causing the motor rotor to dominate joint acceleration in high-ratio gearboxes ($N \in [50, 160]$), rendering transmissions non-backdrivable under impact and bounding reactive disturbance rejection unless closed-loop sensing responds within sub-millisecond loops (@sec-body).
* **The Unified Stopping Distance and Real-Time Latency Budget**: Unifying optical sensor exposure, SerDes serialization, PCIe direct memory access (DMA) transfers, neural inference tail latency, fieldbus jitter (CAN-FD, EtherCAT), microcontroller timer jitter, gate-driver rise time, motor inductive lag ($L/R$), and Coulomb braking into an unrecoverable spatial stopping budget ($d_{\text{stop}} \approx v \tau_{\text{delay}} + \frac{v^2}{2 a_{\text{brake}}}$). Recognizing that delay is physical distance traveled toward an obstacle (@sec-boundary, @sec-body, @sec-nervous, @sec-enforcement).
* **Power Electronics, Inverter Bridges, Phase Currents, and Thermal Ceilings**: Three-phase inverter bridge topologies, pulse-width modulation (PWM) switching at 10–20 kHz, field-oriented control (FOC), irreversible Joule heating in motor stator windings ($P = I_{\text{phase}}^2 R_{\text{phase}}$), thermal time constants ($\Delta T = P \cdot R_{\text{th}}$), and power delivery network (PDN) inductive voltage droop ($V_{\text{sag}} = L_{\text{cable}} \frac{di}{dt}$) during transient torque surges (@sec-body, @sec-nervous, @sec-placement).
* **Endogenous Causality and Compounding Covariate Shift**: Formulating training, data collection, and evaluation for systems whose own actions dictate future sensory observations ($s_{t+1} \sim P(s \mid s_t, a_t)$). Analyzing why batching across time is impossible (collapsing batch size to $B=1$), why imitation learning errors compound quadratically over the planning horizon ($\mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon)$, @sec-boundary-bedrock-laws), and why static offline validation benchmarks fail to predict closed-loop physical survival (@sec-data, @sec-training, @sec-evaluation).
* **The Proposal-Permission Architecture and Safety Certificates**: Deconstructing monolithic policies into an unprivileged cognitive proposer (the Brain) and a deterministic, hard real-time permission path (the Nervous System). Formulating Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) and quadratic programs (QPs) evaluated on isolated safety microcontrollers at 100–500 Hz to guarantee forward invariance of safe sets without relying on neural policy correctness (@sec-boundary, @sec-brain, @sec-nervous, @sec-enforcement).
* **Multi-Rate Heterogeneous Runtime Systems and Silicon Contention**: Orchestrating execution across timescales spanning four orders of magnitude: semantic scene understanding at 1–5 Hz, trajectory chunking at 10–30 Hz, safety barrier filtering at 100–500 Hz, and motor inverter field-oriented control at 10–20 kHz; resolving system-on-chip (SoC) memory crossbar contention, bus arbitration jitter, and DMA starvation between 100 TOPS neural processing units and deterministic real-time microcontrollers (@sec-placement).
* **Supervisory Authority Handovers and Reversible Transitions**: Designing bumpless authority transfers between autonomous policies and human teleoperators, managing cognitive latency floors, initial condition matching, integrator pre-biasing, and discrete temporal leases (@sec-intervention).
* **Evidence-Bound Operational Release and Epistemic Limits**: Grounding system deployment claims in formal limit records, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) fault injection, verifiable operational design domains (ODDs), and accountable residual-claims registers, recognizing that safety guarantees in physical AI are conditional on stated physical premises (@sec-verification, @sec-release, @sec-frontier).

## Curricular Reading Tracks {#sec-prereq-tracks}

To accommodate different course syllabi, research specializations, and engineering roles, this book supports four structured reading tracks:

* **Track 1: The Core Systems Curriculum (Full Sequential Arc)**:
  Designed for semester-long university courses (such as an advanced Physical AI Systems course following CS 288) and practitioners seeking complete mastery of embodied systems architecture. Traces the full four-part sequence: Foundation and Causal Boundary (@sec-boundary) $\to$ The Machine Anatomy (@sec-body, @sec-brain, @sec-nervous) $\to$ Teaching the Machine (@sec-data, @sec-training, @sec-evaluation) $\to$ Running the Machine (@sec-perception, @sec-memory, @sec-intent, @sec-planning, @sec-enforcement, @sec-placement) $\to$ Governing the Machine (@sec-intervention, @sec-verification, @sec-release) $\to$ Capstone Synthesis (@sec-frontier).
* **Track 2: The ML Systems and Learned Runtimes Track (Crossing into Action)**:
  Tailored for machine learning engineers, compiler developers, and runtime researchers focusing on how high-capacity foundation models and generative action chunk decoders interface with physical execution. Emphasizes inference latency budgets, action chunking, endogenous covariate shift, closed-loop policy evaluation, runtime safety filtering, and heterogeneous SoC memory placement: @sec-boundary, @sec-brain, @sec-data, @sec-training, @sec-evaluation, @sec-intent, @sec-planning, @sec-enforcement, @sec-placement, and @sec-frontier.
* **Track 3: The Silicon, RTOS, and Embedded Systems Track (Deterministic Real-Time Heterogeneity)**:
  Tailored for computer architects, embedded systems engineers, and silicon designers managing multi-rate execution across heterogeneous SoCs and real-time microcontrollers. Emphasizes physical plant dynamics, deterministic fieldbuses (CAN-FD, EtherCAT), real-time operating system (RTOS) scheduling and timer jitter, high-speed sensor transport (MIPI CSI-2, SerDes), unified memory bus contention, and safety microcontroller isolation: @sec-boundary, @sec-body, @sec-nervous, @sec-perception, @sec-memory, @sec-enforcement, @sec-placement, and @sec-verification.
* **Track 4: The Robotics, Controls, and Safety Assurance Track (Certifiable Embodied Autonomy)**:
  Tailored for roboticists, control engineers, and safety certifiers integrating stochastic neural proposers into safety-critical physical plants. Emphasizes rigid-body mechanics, foundation model proposers, Control Barrier Functions, bumpless supervisory handovers, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) fault injection, empirical safety cases, and residual risk registers: @sec-boundary, @sec-body, @sec-brain, @sec-planning, @sec-enforcement, @sec-intervention, @sec-verification, @sec-release, and @sec-frontier.

| Track | Primary Audience | Core Chapter Progression | Primary Systems Competency |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Track 1: Core Systems Curriculum** | Graduate students & systems architects | Complete curriculum: @sec-boundary through @sec-frontier (all 17 chapters) | Complete architectural mastery of physical AI machines from physics to governance |

These structured tracks (@tbl-prereq-tracks) complement the sequential curriculum, allowing readers and instructors to navigate this book according to their primary analytical focus while maintaining full architectural context.

## What the Book Introduces

The book starts from the physical and computational relationships needed to explain a system's behavior. Rather than treating physical AI as a disconnected collection of robotics heuristics or deep learning architectures, the curriculum establishes a structured **pedagogical taxonomy** spanning five interconnected systems tiers:

### 1. The physical plant and conservation tier

* **Newtonian Momentum and Stopping Kinematics**: Formulating the unrecoverable stopping distance budget ($d_{\text{stop}} \approx v \tau_{\text{delay}} + \frac{v^2}{2 a_{\text{brake}}}$) under Coulomb friction limits ($\mu g$).
* **Electromagnetic Actuation and Phase Currents**: Three-phase inverter switching (PWM at 10–20 kHz), field-oriented control (FOC), motor torque constants ($k_t$), and back-EMF ($k_b$).
* **Thermodynamic and PDN Limits**: Irreversible Joule heating ($P = I_{\text{phase}}^2 R_{\text{phase}}$), stator thermal dissipation envelopes, and inductive voltage droop ($V_{\text{sag}} = L_{\text{cable}} \frac{di}{dt}$) during transient torque surges.
* **Transmission Dynamics and Reflected Inertia**: Understanding why reflected rotor inertia scales quadratically with gear ratio ($J_{\text{ref}} = N^2 J_{\text{rotor}}$), rendering high-ratio harmonic and cycloidal reducers ($N \in [50, 160]$) non-backdrivable under impact shock.

### 2. The real-time heterogeneous silicon tier

* **Multi-Rate Execution Hierarchy**: Orchestrating concurrent control loops across four orders of magnitude: 1–5 Hz semantic intent, 10–30 Hz action chunking, 100–500 Hz safety barrier filtering, and 10–20 kHz motor field-oriented control.
* **SoC Memory Crossbar Isolation**: Managing unified memory bus contention, bus arbitration latency, and DMA starvation between 100 TOPS neural processing units and deterministic real-time cores.
* **Deterministic Fieldbuses and Transport**: Hard real-time sensor and actuator networking over CAN-FD and EtherCAT, alongside high-speed camera serialization over MIPI CSI-2 and SerDes links.

### 3. The cognitive learning and action generation tier

* **Continuous Action Spaces and Trajectory Chunking**: Generating multi-step temporal action chunks to overcome single-step autoregressive latency bottlenecks.
* **Generative Diffusion and Flow-Matching Policies**: Decoding multimodal action trajectories under strict real-time denoising deadlines.
* **Endogenous Data and Compounding Error**: Addressing quadratic error accumulation ($\mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon)$) under closed-loop distribution shift ($s_{t+1} \sim P(s \mid s_t, a_t)$) without relying on static test benchmarks.
* **Inference Batch Size $B=1$ Optimization**: Structuring neural runtimes for strictly non-batchable real-time execution.

### 4. The deterministic safety and enforcement tier

* **The Proposal-Permission Separation**: Architecturally isolating untrusted, high-capacity neural proposers (the Brain) from physical actuation authority.
* **Control Barrier Functions (CBFs)**: Defining forward-invariant safe sets ($\mathcal{C}$) based on physical kinematic and dynamic state constraints.
* **Real-Time Quadratic Program (QP) Filtering**: Minimally projecting learned action proposals onto admissible safety sets at 100–500 Hz on isolated safety silicon.
* **Deterministic Emergency Fallbacks**: Fail-safe stopping and graceful degradation paths that activate when real-time deadlines or invariant bounds are breached.

### 5. The epistemic governance and verification tier

* **Supervisory Human-Machine Handovers**: Designing bumpless authority transitions, cognitive latency floor buffers, and discrete temporal leases.
* **Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Fault Injection**: Stress-testing policies and safety filters against simulated sensor dropouts, bus latency tail spikes, and actuator saturation.
* **Limit Records and Residual Claims**: Grounding operational deployment in formal, empirical limit records and explicit residual-claims registers rather than open-ended statistical extrapolation.

Detailed proofs, specialized notation, and wire-format data structures provide optional depth in the systems appendices. The main text retains the physical mechanism, underlying assumptions, and engineering consequences so that following the systems argument does not depend on prior specialist training.

## How to Read the Numbers {#sec-reader-numbers}

Every number in this book carries one of five labels, four categories of evidence and one for design choices, and its label decides what it may be used for:

* **Measured**: A calibrated observation of a particular machine. It names its instrument, its operating conditions, its sample count, and, for a distribution, the percentile it reports. Only a measured number, or a number derived from measured ones, can support a safety margin.
* **Derived**: Computed from measured numbers through a stated physical or statistical model. It carries that model's assumptions and the propagated uncertainty of its inputs.
* **Datasheet**: A manufacturer's rating under the manufacturer's conditions. It says what to expect and what to test, and it is not evidence about the unit on the bench.
* **Illustrative**: Selected to show arithmetic or scaling. It supports no margin, timeout, or release decision.

A budget or requirement, such as a lease duration or a clearance margin, belongs to none of the four. It is a design decision, labeled **chosen**, and it means something only when it is checked against the measured or derived number it must fit, as a chosen lease is checked against the derived ceiling on pre-brake delay.

A worked design in this book shows a decision procedure. When its inputs are illustrative, the decision it reaches is illustrative too. It shows how the machine's speed, lease, or verdict would be set, and it would bind a real machine only after the inputs it names are measured.

When a number decides something, such as a speed limit, a timeout, or a release, the book keeps it as a **limit record** with six elements: the value or distribution; the operating conditions under which it holds (payload, temperature, supply voltage, surface, concurrent workload, firmware); the measurement uncertainty; the engineering margin between the operating target and the breakdown threshold; the detector that catches an excursion while the machine runs; and its provenance, meaning its label and the instrument or model that produced it. A limit holds only under its stated conditions. When wear, heat, a new payload, or a new build changes them, the limit must be established again before it is reused.

Worked examples label each number's category once, at first use. A result holds under the assumptions stated with its example and nowhere else. A bound from finitely many trials holds under its sampling assumptions and proves nothing beyond them, and a measured percentile describes the tested workload, not a worst case. In a release argument each premise also has a status: established (measured or derived), assumed, decided by accountable judgment, unsupported, or outside the threat model. @Sec-release and @sec-frontier use these statuses.

## What We Deliberately Omit

The book focuses on how learned computation, physical mechanisms, and execution systems work together. That focus limits the depth of its treatment in neighboring fields:

* **Exhaustive Robotic Kinematic Derivations**: We do not derive symbolic Denavit-Hartenberg parameter tables or catalog forward and inverse kinematics for dozens of specialized manipulator geometries. The relevant systems concern is how degrees of freedom, kinematic reach, and actuator torque limits constrain the physical workspace and stopping envelope.
* **Abstract Deep Learning Optimization Theory**: We do not explore loss surface geometry, theoretical generalization bounds, or speculative convergence proofs. Machine learning mechanisms are examined where their computational structure, memory footprint, or sampling latency directly binds the real-time execution budget.
* **Transient Software Framework and Middleware Tutorials**: We do not provide user tutorials for specific robotics middleware packages or proprietary simulation environments. Software is treated through its underlying systems primitives: zero-copy ring buffers, inter-process communication (IPC), shared-memory mailboxes, clock synchronization protocols, and DMA engines that any production runtime must manage.

These boundaries leave the essential mechanisms and their consequences in the systems argument. They limit exhaustive specialist treatment without making familiarity with that treatment a prerequisite for following the book.
